newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CIVIL AVIATION ENGINEERS CALL STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CIVIL AVIATION ENGINEERS CALL STRIKE.

text.p: Greek civil aviation electrical engineers are on strike from February 17 to 21 protesting against the government's new bill on civil servant wages, they said in a statement on Tuesday.
Their strike will last from 2300 GMT on Monday to 2200 GMT on Friday, their union said.

"We are fighting against the abolition of our information technology bonus, granted to us since 1989. We now handle larger electronic systems but are faced with the oxymoron of having this bonus eliminated," Athanassios Kyriazis, the union's president told Reuters.
Transport and Communications Minister Haralambos Kastanidis, had agreed in mid-January to take care of this issue, Kyriazis said.
"We expected the minister to have done something by now. We also informed him of this new strike last Monday so that there would be ample time for reconsideration," he said.
In terms of passenger convenience, the strike means there could be flight delays or cancellations as air traffic controllers will have less electronic means to perform their jobs, Kyriazis said.

"However, the safety of flights is not put in jeopardy. Passengers could only be faced with cancellations or delays that will become worse with the passing of each additional day, as more and more electrical devices will be unavailable," he said.
Airport officials said the only delay on Monday was in the afternoon flight from Athens to the Greek island of Rhodes. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
